configuration: Section 3.4 'Proactive Agent' as run inside the Environment Gym (repo gym/ package: ProactiveAgent, EnvironmentStateManager and UserAgent sharing one codelinker EventSink), with retained event/dialogue history for one scenario run and simulated accepted-task execution (ProactiveAgent.exec). Both judgment paths were considered: default LLM user-agent judgment and the USE_ACTIVERM reward-model judgment path described in Sec. 3.4 ('feedback from the user agent on its draft prediction'). The deployed desktop app under agent/ and the offline training scripts were read only to delimit scope.
sources_read: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.12361v3 (Sections 3.1-3.5, 4.1-4.3, Conclusion/Limitations, Figure 2 and 3 captions, Appendix A/B; read through WebFetch copy-outs; Section 3.4 wording confirmed identical across three independent copy-outs: arxiv HTML twice and ar5iv)
https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.12361v3 (fetched, but PDF could not be rendered locally)
codelinker dependency (installed in cases/proactive-agent/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/codelinker): events/sink.py, events/processer.py, models/sink.py

S->M.label: reported
S->M.rationale: Memory in this configuration is the shared codelinker EventSink (all_events list retained for the whole scenario run). Sensed events generated by the gym are appended to it (environment.py:154 adds each event to sinkChannels.events; EventSink.add appends to self.all_events at sink.py:230 regardless of the silent flag), as are the user agent's judgments on proposals (user.py:143-144). The ProactiveAgent later gathers these retained entries (activeagent.py:111-115). The paper states the same memory update explicitly.
S->M.locator: Paper Sec. 3.4 para. 1 and Figure 3 caption; gym/components/environment.py:148-154; gym/components/user.py:143-144; codelinker/events/sink.py:219-233; gym/components/activeagent.py:111-121
S->M.quote: Paper 3.4: "upon the agent receiving new event E_t at time t, it first updates its memory with the event." Figure 3: "The agent monitors new events and updates its memory to predict potential tasks." Code environment.py:154: self.add(tags=sinkChannels.events, content=eve.event)

M->A.label: reported
M->A.rationale: Retained history (events, prior agent proposals, user judgments, available ops) is gathered from the sink and passed as the message history to the LLM call that decides whether to propose a task or stay silent (activeagent.py:111-130, messages=self.memory + hist) and to the call that chooses the next execution action (activeagent.py:67-74). The system prompt ties the decision to history. The paper states that new events are combined with historical ones and conversations to raise tasks.
M->A.locator: Paper Sec. 3.4 para. 1; gym/components/activeagent.py:28, 33, 67-74, 111-130; codelinker/events/processer.py:55-89 (gather returns the retained sink entries)
M->A.quote: Paper 3.4: "Combining new events with historical ones and conversations with the user, the agent incorporates user characteristics to raise potential tasks." Code activeagent.py:28: "- Deduce the user's purpose and whether they need help based on event history." activeagent.py:129: messages=self.memory + hist

A->S.label: reported
A->S.rationale: Action state and intentions guide what the agent senses. (1) Expected-effect check on a draft: the agent raises a proposal and waits for the judgment on that proposal before proceeding (step() waits on the proactive channel, activeagent.py:104; exec() is triggered by the judgment, :60); in the USE_ACTIVERM path the draft itself is submitted for judgment and the returned verdict/thought drives a retry (activeagent.py:137-155). The paper states both the wait-for-judgment and feedback-on-draft. (2) Execution state gates acquisition: while executing an accepted task the agent unregisters its event-prediction listener (activeagent.py:64), skips event steps while the execution lock is held (:101-103), and after each action waits for the gym to process that action before gathering the resulting events (:84-86); the paper describes the agent detecting the new state after each of its actions.
A->S.locator: Paper Sec. 3.4 para. 1 and 'Task Execution' paragraph; gym/components/activeagent.py:59-60, 62-64, 80, 84-86, 101-104, 137-155
A->S.quote: Paper 3.4: "If the agent detects potential tasks, it will raise the task as a new event and wait for the judgment of the user agent." / "To improve the quality of the prediction, it also accepts feedback from the user agent on its draft prediction." / Task Execution: "After that, the proactive agent detects the new environment state S_{t+1} and takes new actions according to the events generated by the gym." Code activeagent.py:64: self.unlisten(self.step); :86: await self.wait(sinkChannels.activity); :137: res = await rm.judge(pred.get("Proactive Task", None))

M->S.label: insufficient
M->S.rationale: No described mechanism supplies retained priors to sampling, attention, or compression: the agent gathers every retained event unconditionally (activeagent.py:111-115) and passes raw events to the model. The only candidate is the single fused prediction call, whose prompt asks for the 'Purpose' of the user's last action deduced from event history while also producing the task decision; the source does not separate this interpretation from the answer-time decision, so a distinct memory-to-Sensing link is not established. The paper frames history use only as raising tasks (M->A). Not explicitly excluded, so not 'absent'.
M->S.quote: Code activeagent.py:17: "Purpose": "The purpose of the user's last action." (produced in the same JSON as "Proactive Task" by one call at :126-130)

A->M.label: reported
A->M.rationale: The agent's own outputs are written into the shared retained store and re-read later: every prediction (including silent no-task predictions) is added to the agent.proactive channel (activeagent.py:174; EventSink.add appends before the silent check, sink.py:227-233), execution actions are added to the activity channel (activeagent.py:84), and accepted predictions with their context are stored on agent.response (:172). On later steps gather() returns the agent's own entries as assistant-role messages (processer.py:83-85) which step() folds into hist (activeagent.py:116-119). The paper states that a detected task is raised as a new event and that conversations with the user are combined with history.
A->M.locator: Paper Sec. 3.4 para. 1; gym/components/activeagent.py:84, 116-119, 172, 174; codelinker/events/sink.py:227-233; codelinker/events/processer.py:83-85
A->M.quote: Code activeagent.py:174: self.add(sinkChannels.agent.proactive, content=json.dumps(pred),silent=pred.get("Proactive Task", None) is None). Paper 3.4: "it will raise the task as a new event and wait for the judgment of the user agent."

record.label: stated
record.rationale: The agent stores each decision it makes (task proposal or null) and each execution action in the run's shared EventSink and reads them back on subsequent steps as its own assistant turns; this is in-run use by the service, not only an author log. The out_file JSONL (gym/main.py:24-32) is additionally written for the authors but is not what establishes the step.
record.locator: gym/components/activeagent.py:84, 116-119, 174; codelinker/events/sink.py:230; codelinker/events/processer.py:83-85; Paper Sec. 3.4 para. 1
record.quote: Code activeagent.py:174: self.add(sinkChannels.agent.proactive, content=json.dumps(pred),silent=pred.get("Proactive Task", None) is None); activeagent.py:116-119: if e['role'] == 'assistant': ... hist.append(e)

outcome.label: stated
outcome.rationale: The simulated user's accept/reject judgment on each proposal is written to the shared sink (user.py:143-144) and is gathered by the agent on later steps (activeagent.py:67-68, 111-115); the gym's events describing the effects of the agent's execution actions are likewise retained in the events channel (environment.py:141-154). In the USE_ACTIVERM path the reward-model verdict and its reasoning are obtained directly (activeagent.py:137, 143).
outcome.locator: gym/components/user.py:117-146; gym/components/activeagent.py:67-68, 111-115, 137-143; gym/components/environment.py:121-154; Paper Sec. 3.4 para. 1
outcome.quote: Code user.py:143-144: self.add(tags=sinkChannels.agent.proactive, content=f"{res.thought}\nIs Accepted: {res.is_accepted}"). Paper 3.4: "wait for the judgment of the user agent."

attribution.label: stated
attribution.rationale: The judgment is tied to the specific proposal and used to correct or gate assistance: with USE_ACTIVERM the rejected draft is re-sent as 'Previous Prediction' with 'Status': 'Rejected' and the judge's 'User Feedback', and the agent must produce a different prediction (activeagent.py:139-155); in the default path the execution prompt instructs the agent to take no action if the user rejects the proposal (activeagent.py:43) and the judgment immediately follows the proposal in the gathered history. The paper states that feedback on the draft prediction is used to improve it.
attribution.locator: gym/components/activeagent.py:43, 139-159; Paper Sec. 3.4 para. 1; Paper Sec. 4.3 (reward-model feedback setting)
attribution.quote: Code activeagent.py:141-144: step_obj["Previous Prediction"] = pred / step_obj["Status"] = "Rejected" / step_obj["User Feedback"] = res.thought / step_obj["Instructions"] = f"Your previous prediction is rejected! You must make a different prediction." Paper 3.4: "To improve the quality of the prediction, it also accepts feedback from the user agent on its draft prediction."

revision.label: not_stated
revision.rationale: Within the gym run nothing durable about the mechanism changes: the system prompt is a constant (activeagent.py:54-56), the model is fixed by private.toml, and the retry loop only alters the current prediction (content), not a rule, prompt, or parameters. The only mechanism change in the work is offline fine-tuning of LLaMA-3.1-8B/Qwen2-7B by the authors on gym-generated data via dataset/build_agent_trainset.py and LLaMA-Factory (Sec. 4.2, Appendix B), which is a developer-made change, not a self-revision by the service.
revision.locator: gym/components/activeagent.py:54-56, 139-155; dataset/build_agent_trainset.py:196-238; dataset/README.md 'Build the Proactive Agent Trainset'; Paper Sec. 4.2 and Appendix B

revision.what: None in-service. The only revised artifacts are model weights fine-tuned offline by the authors (LLaMA-3.1-8B-Proactive, Qwen2-7B-Proactive); developer-made, so not counted.

later_use.label: not_stated
later_use.rationale: No self-made revision exists, so no later run under a self-revised mechanism is reported. The fine-tuned models were evaluated on ProactiveBench (Sec. 4.2, Table 3; README results table), but that is use of a developer-trained model, not later use of a revision made by the service.

notes: Judged the Sec. 3.4 agent as instantiated in gym/ at commit 3fcf9be. Memory is the shared codelinker EventSink retained for one scenario run (no cross-run persistence is reloaded; the out_file JSONL is only written). Paper quotes for Sec. 3.4 were confirmed identical across three independent copy-outs (arxiv HTML v3 twice via WebFetch, plus ar5iv); Bash was unavailable and the PDF could not be rendered, so one Sec. 4.2 quote from a single copy-out is marked UNVERIFIED. Code quotes were read directly from the files. The reward-model path (USE_ACTIVERM) is treated as part of the configuration because Sec. 3.4 describes feedback on the draft prediction; the default path (LLM user-agent judgment) supports the same channel and step labels except that attribution there is by prompt instruction and adjacency rather than an explicit 'Previous Prediction' field. The deployed agent/ app (README mentions reducing proposals after ignores) is outside this configuration and was not used for any label.
